verses.text: Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew his time had come to leave this world and go to the Father. He had loved his own people in the world, and he loved them all the way through.
Dinner was underway. The devil had already put the idea of betraying Jesus into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son.
Jesus knew the Father had put everything into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God.
So he got up from the meal, took off his outer clothes, and wrapped a towel around his waist.
Then he poured water into a basin and began washing the disciples’ feet, drying them with the towel around him. 💧
When he came to Simon Peter, Peter asked, “Lord, you’re going to wash my feet?”
Jesus answered, “You don’t understand what I’m doing right now, but you’ll understand later.”
Peter said, “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus replied, “If I don’t wash you, you have no share with me.”
Simon Peter said, “Lord, then wash my hands and head too—not just my feet!”
Jesus said, “Someone who has bathed only needs their feet washed; they’re already clean all over. You are clean, but not all of you.”
Jesus knew who was going to betray him. That was why he said, “Not all of you are clean.”
After washing their feet, Jesus put his outer clothes back on and sat down again. “Do you understand what I’ve done for you?” he asked.
“You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you’re right—that’s who I am.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, washed your feet, you should wash one another’s feet too.
I’ve given you an example. Do for each other what I’ve done for you.
I’m telling you the truth: a servant isn’t greater than the master, and a messenger isn’t greater than the one who sent them.
Now that you know this, you’ll be blessed if you put it into practice.
I’m not talking about all of you. I know the people I chose. But Scripture must come true: ‘The one who shares my bread has turned against me.’
I’m telling you this before it happens, so when it does happen, you’ll believe that I am he.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever welcomes someone I send welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes the One who sent me.”
After saying this, Jesus was deeply troubled. He told them plainly, “I’m telling you the truth: one of you will betray me.”
The disciples looked at one another, confused about who he meant.
One of the disciples Jesus loved was at the table, leaning against his chest.
Simon Peter gestured to him and said, “Ask him who he means.”
So that disciple leaned back toward Jesus and asked, “Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answered, “It’s the one I give this piece of bread to after I dip it.” Then he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son.
After Judas took the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, “What you’re going to do, do quickly.”
Nobody else at the table understood why Jesus said that to him.
Some thought that, since Judas kept the money bag, Jesus was telling him, “Buy what we need for the festival,” or to give something to the poor.
Judas took the bread and went out right away. It was night.
When Judas had gone, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.
If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself—and do it right away.
Children, I will be with you only a little longer. You will look for me. As I told the Jewish leaders, you cannot come where I am going; now I tell you the same.
Here’s a new command I’m giving you: love one another. Love each other the way I have loved you. ❤️
Everyone will know you’re my disciples by this: you love one another.”
Simon Peter asked him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “You can’t follow me now, but you will follow later.”
Peter said, “Lord, why can’t I follow you now? I’ll give my life for you.”
Jesus answered, “You’ll give your life for me? I’m telling you the truth: the rooster won’t crow until you’ve denied me three times.”
